title: Wall-clock timing assertion is an intermittency risk
evidence: acceptance_test.go:174-178 TestShouldAnswerAggregateQuestionsQuickly asserts ThenAnswerArrivedWithinSeconds(5); dsl_test.go:81-86 fails on elapsed wall-clock. On a loaded CI box this flakes while nothing is broken.
suggestion: Move the performance check out of the behaviour suite, or make it a generous catastrophic-regression ceiling (tens of seconds), not a 5s SLA inside a functional spec.

title: Acceptance assertions coupled to rendered output format and CSV filenames
evidence: acceptance_test.go:78 asserts '1. Flamengo - 90 pts'; :66 'Matches: 19'; :161-166 asserts raw CSV filenames (Brasileirao_Matches.csv ...). A formatter change or a different backing store breaks green tests though behaviour is unchanged.
suggestion: Push formatting into DSL/PD outcome methods (ThenChampionIs, ThenPointsFor, ThenDataCovers) and assert domain outcomes, not rendered strings.

title: Specs pinned to a large shared fixture with no functional isolation
evidence: driver_test.go:30-34 loads the whole data/kaggle dataset once; specs assert exact snapshot values (acceptance_test.go:102 '1. Neymar Jr - Overall: 92'). Refreshing the Kaggle CSVs would break specs for reasons unrelated to correctness. (Read-only data mitigates cross-test interference.)
suggestion: Narrow each spec to the single relationship it is about (e.g. ThenTopResultIs, ThenResultsAreRankedByRatingDescending) to shrink the blast radius of dataset refreshes.

title: A few specs assert more than one outcome
evidence: acceptance_test.go:20-26 TestShouldFindCopaDoBrasilFinals and :129-135 TestShouldCompareTwoSeasons each do two When/Then cycles in one test.
suggestion: Split into single-outcome specs per lesson 305 ('assert a single outcome').
